text: Over the last few decades. <break time="0.8s" /> Public interest in hunger artists. <break time="0.8s" /> Has dwindled sharply. <break time="0.8s" /> And an exhibition of fasting. <break time="0.8s" /> That once filled a showmans pockets. <break time="0.8s" /> Would today attract hardly anyone at all. <break time="0.8s" /> There was a time, however. <break time="0.8s" /> When the whole town took part in the spectacle. <break time="0.8s" /> And as the fast went on people came daily. <break time="0.8s" /> Some buying season tickets. <break time="0.8s" /> To sit before the little barred cage all day long. <break time="0.8s" /> Even at night visitors came to view him by torchlight. <break time="0.8s" /> And on fine days. <break time="0.8s" /> The cage was carried into the open air. <break time="0.8s" /> Where the children above all. <break time="0.8s" /> Stared at him in open mouthed wonder. <break time="0.8s" /> To the adults. <break time="0.8s" /> He was often just a fashionable joke. <break time="0.8s" /> But the children. <break time="0.8s" /> Holding hands for safety. <break time="0.8s" /> Gazed in amazement at the pale figure. <break time="0.8s" /> In black tights. <break time="0.8s" /> His ribs sticking out sharply. <break time="0.8s" /> Sitting on the scattered straw. <break time="0.8s" /> Scorning even a chair. <break time="0.8s" /> He sometimes nodded politely. <break time="0.8s" /> And answered questions with a strained smile. <break time="0.8s" /> Or he stretched an arm through the bars. <break time="0.8s" /> So that people could feel how thin it was before sinking back into himself again. <break time="0.8s" /> Then he would ignore everyone. <break time="0.8s" /> Even the striking of the clock. <break time="0.8s" /> That was the cages only furniture. <break time="0.8s" /> And simply stare ahead. <break time="0.8s" /> With half closed eyes. <break time="0.8s" /> Now and then sipping water. <break time="0.8s" /> From a tiny glass to moisten his lips. <break time="0.8s" /> Besides the changing crowds. <break time="0.8s" /> There were also permanent watchers. <break time="0.8s" /> Chosen by the public. <break time="0.8s" /> Usually butchers, oddly enough. <break time="0.8s" /> Who in teams of three. <break time="0.8s" /> Kept their eyes on him day and night. <break time="0.8s" /> So that he could not secretly take any food. <break time="0.8s" /> This was, however. <break time="0.8s" /> Merely a formality. <break time="0.8s" /> Introduced to reassure the masses. <break time="0.8s" /> For those who understood the art. <break time="0.8s" /> Knew well. <break time="0.8s" /> That during his fast. <break time="0.8s" /> The hunger artist would never swallow. <break time="0.8s" /> Even the smallest crumb. <break time="0.8s" /> Not even if forced.
